persons.name: Bora Özkent
persons.digest: In this video Bora Özkent assesses Tesla's Roadster unveiling from both a technology and an investment angle. **Tesla** drove the Roadster on the ceiling, flipped it in mid-air and took it from 0 to 100 km/h in 0.81 seconds, while production has slipped to 2028. Bora sees it as a strong showcase and branding exercise pointing to a **Tesla**-**SpaceX** merger rather than a commercial product, yet grants both the bull and bear arguments. He says the Roadster will be a tiny share of Tesla's total sales, that US credit markets are under some stress, and that investors are now checking whether companies will actually make money.

items.title: Tesla Resmen Uçtu!
items.summary: Bora describes the Roadster demo in which the car drove on the ceiling, flipped mid-air and jumped over a truck; the headline numbers are 0-100 km/h in 0.81 s, a 370 km/h top speed, fan-suction grip of up to 2G and a 2028 production date. There are three versions: Performance (0-100 in 1.6 s), Thrust and the SpaceX-thruster Rocket; a place in line costs roughly a $250k deposit. The Roadster was first shown in 2017 and was due in 2020; the slip to 2028 is the part he believes least. He sees it as a technology showcase rather than a commercial product, a strong sign of a Tesla-SpaceX merger and a branding exercise. Tesla sold 1.6 million cars last year and the Roadster will be a very small slice. The stock was slightly positive early, but he doubts how lasting the rally is; with stress in US credit markets investors are looking at whether companies will really make money. Regulator reaction, physical limits and recharging remain open questions. He adds that Tesla's auto business is doing fine thanks to fuel prices, autonomy progress and the Model Y being China's best-selling EV.

assets.note: Sees the Roadster as a great showcase and branding effort but with no commercial boost to the company, production in 2028 and a poor Musk track record; grants both the bull and bear readings.
Sees it as a clear sign Tesla and SpaceX could merge later; the car's thrusters come from SpaceX.

He said he has been unable to reach money sitting in a PPF for a month, that SPK has made no statement, and argued funds took liquid cash against poor collateral. After MSCI paused Turkey index changes, he wrote that even with regulation introduced foreigners will assume it can happen again. He also joked about the **SOXX** ETF landing in the middle of portfolios.

items.title: Who guarantees it won't happen again after MSCI?
items.summary: dtfinans_ wrote that relief after regulation and MSCI saying fine isn't enough, asked whether the SPK can guarantee it won't happen again, and said foreigners will see that if it happened once it can happen again.

assets.note: Foreign investors will assume that if it happened once it can happen again.

persons.name: WallStDiaries
persons.digest: WallStDiaries' day revolved around the AI sell-off and credit worries: chip stocks are in their worst losing streak since 2008 (**SOXX**), and **CoreWeave**'s debt plus a credit crisis in neocloud bonds rattled the bond market too. September PPI at 1.3% monthly leaves the Fed in a bind, while MSCI-driven passive selling risk of about $2.8B for **Strategy**, **Microsoft**'s FCF edge, **Varonis**'s $6.3B takeover and **Tesla**'s new Roadster were the notable company stories. The US budget deficit rose to $1.99 trillion.

items.title: Chip stocks' worst losing streak since 2008
items.summary: Chip stocks have fallen eight straight sessions with nearly $2 trillion erased; doubts about AI spending returns and high rates are blamed.

assets.note: Worst losing streak since 2008.

items.title: MSCI inactive-company rule could hit MSTR
items.summary: MSCI is removing companies with limited operations from its indexes; Strategy could face about $2.8B of forced passive selling, with the final list due November 11.

assets.note: About $2.8B of forced passive selling pressure.

items.title: CoreWeave's debt bind
items.summary: CoreWeave's roughly $50B of debt and bond yields above 16% raise doubts about data-center spending sustainability.

assets.note: About $50B of debt with bond yields above 16%.

items.title: Neocloud alarm in bonds
items.summary: Treasury yields fell sharply but the cause is a credit crisis in neocloud bonds; Oracle and CoreWeave CDS spreads are at records.

CDS spread at a record.

persons.name: FinancewithIzzy
persons.digest: FinancewithIzzy reads this week's AI sell-off through rates and debt: the US deficit rising to $1.99 trillion pushes up bond supply and long-term yields and hits AI and tech stocks, and **CoreWeave** falling 15% then rising 6% on Jensen Huang's words is fragility, not a bottom. He infers from Fed Chair Warsh's remark that AI could push prices up near term that a rate hike is not off the table; the October 28 FOMC is key. He also relayed Taiwan making chip smuggling a crime and the 11% drop in Indonesia after MSCI.

items.title: US budget deficit nears $2 trillion
items.summary: The deficit rose to $1.99T (+12%); spending grew over 5% and revenue 3%. A bigger deficit means more bond supply and higher long-term yields, hitting AI and tech stocks.

items.title: Wall Street is split
items.summary: BofA/Hartnett says stay away from risk and Barclays says the best of the AI rally may be behind while Goldman, UBS and Citi see opportunity in some sectors; FinancewithIzzy wrote it is time to bet on the right stock, not the wave.

items.title: Smuggling AI chips from Taiwan to China will become a crime
items.summary: According to Taiwan's Economy Minister, AI servers and advanced chips are going on the control list and shipping banned hardware to China will be a crime under the Foreign Trade Act.

items.title: Huang spoke one sentence, CoreWeave jumped 6%
items.summary: CoreWeave fell 15.5% on Wednesday and rose 5.9% on Friday on Huang's remarks; FinancewithIzzy wrote that Nvidia is both supplier and shareholder, that this is a fragility signal rather than a bottom, and that the October 28 FOMC comes first. Indonesian stocks fell 11% on the MSCI decision.

assets.note: Fell 15% on a bond yield and rose 6% on a CEO sentence; a fragility signal, not a bottom.
Nvidia is both CoreWeave's supplier and shareholder, so Huang's words aren't neutral.

persons.digest: jrouldz wrote that on the down day he is trying not to catch falling knives, and lamented the "dead cat bounce" crowd being right. He said **MP Materials** is the safer bet while **USAR** is higher risk/reward, and that he finds it hard to sell **CrowdStrike** and **Cloudflare** despite obscene valuations. persons.name: cevikfinance
persons.digest: cevikfinance reads the sell-off through technical and sentiment gauges: he wrote that AI infrastructure, semiconductor, optics, memory and space themes fell about 18% on the week, yet the **VIX** hasn't reached panic levels and SKEW last hit these levels before the 2021 bear market and the 2025 tariff shock. On **NDX** the first support is 28,650, then the 50-week average at 27,500 and 26,000, and he says the Nasdaq weekly chart resembles the setups before the February 2025 and February 2026 declines. He read Bank of America's AI boom-bust warning as adding fuel to the fire, and said of **Rocket Lab**'s chart that we should have seen it coming in May.

items.title: NDX levels at 28,650, 27,500 and 26,000
items.summary: cevikfinance wrote that NDX is nearing first support at 28,650, with room to the 50-week average at 27,500 and then the 2025 high at 26,000 if it fails, unless Trump steps in, and that the weekly chart resembles the setups before February 2025/2026.

assets.note: First support 28,650, then 27,500 and 26,000.

holdings.name: SoFi Technologies
holdings.opinion: The portfolio's largest holding (18%); fintech stocks stay volatile on rate-hike odds and credit-quality worries. What matters is credit losses and the effect of higher rates on funding costs.
ai_points: For: no negative news on SoFi in today's sources.
Against: an 18% weight is concentration risk, and the rate-hike odds (17.2%) after hot PPI can weigh on such stocks.
Against: stress in credit markets is a risk for fintech lenders.

mentions.quote: While rivals such as Alphabet, Amazon and Meta see serious contractions and even negative levels in free cash flow (FCF)

holdings.why: According to WallStDiaries AI spending is shrinking Meta's free cash flow sharply, but there is no level or date to act on.
holdings.opinion: The portfolio's second-largest holding; AI capex worries and the chip sell-off bear directly on the stock. What matters is spending discipline and the resilience of ad revenue.
ai_points: Against: WallStDiaries expects a sharp free-cash-flow contraction.
For: ad revenue remains a strong cash engine.
Against: a 14% weight makes the portfolio volatile if the tech sell-off continues.

holdings.name: Broadcom

mentions.quote: The company assessed as part of a huge $35 billion financing package backed by Broadcom infrastructure

holdings.why: The chip sell-off continues but the sources give no Broadcom-specific level or change of view.
holdings.opinion: One of the holdings most exposed to the chip sell-off; the Anthropic financing relayed by WallStDiaries rests on Broadcom infrastructure, showing demand is real. The main risk is deterioration in the credit market that funds AI spending.
ai_points: For: per WallStDiaries Anthropic's $35B financing is backed by Broadcom infrastructure.
Against: chip stocks are in their worst losing streak since 2008.
Against: neocloud credit stress threatens the financing of AI demand.

holdings.name: BWX Technologies

Against: broad risk aversion can hit the nuclear theme too.

For: data licensing and ad revenue are income streams independent of AI stocks.
Against: a 9% weight raises single-stock risk.

Against: profit-taking has started in the AI energy rally.
Against: neocloud credit stress could slow data-center investment.

holdings.name: iShares USD Treasury Bond 20+yr EUR Hedged (Dist)

holdings.why: WallStDiaries says the yield drop stems from a credit crisis, but there is no level or date for the bond.

Against: per FinancewithIzzy the $1.99T deficit can push bond supply and long yields up.
